children: Colombia's fiscal deficit is projected to exceed government targets in 2026 and 2027, according to a report by the country's independent fiscal watchdog (CARF) released on Wednesday.

CARF expects a total deficit of 7.8% of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2026 and 9.5% in 2027. Those figures surpass estimates from the administration of President Abelardo De La Espriella, who took office in August, of 7.2% and 9.4% for the respective years.
The committee also projected weaker economic growth than the government, forecasting GDP expansion of 2.5% in 2026 and 1.8% in 2027. The government expects growth of 2.6% and 2.2% for those periods.
